subject: Cognitive Science
title: Fundamental Attribution Error
description: A quick, practical guide to Fundamental Attribution Error.

hook.text: Someone cuts you off in traffic. "What a jerk!" But when you cut someone off, you had a good reason.

buildup.text: The fundamental attribution error: we blame others' behavior on character but our own on circumstances.

discovery.text: Lee Ross named it in 1977. We overweight personality and underweight the situation others are in.

twist.text: It's weaker in collectivist cultures. East Asian participants consider context more than Westerners do.

climax.text: At work, it creates toxic judgment: a missed deadline becomes a character flaw, not a resource problem.

punchline.text: Before judging character, check the situation.

quiz.question: What is the fundamental attribution error?
options: Blaming others' actions on character, not situation
Always seeing the best in others
